run.question: We're running low on disk space. Can you check our application indexes (app-187-*) and identify which one is consuming the most storage? Please tell me the index name and approximately how much space it's using.

report.summary: Among the application indices matching app-187-*, the one using the most storage is app-187-metrics-analytics. At the moment of the query it held 5,000 documents in 1 segment with a store size of 520,263 bytes (about 508 KB, primary and total equal on a single-node cluster). The other 20 indices, app-187-logs-01 through app-187-logs-20, each held 10 documents and about 9 KB, so the analytics index is roughly 55x the size of any single logs index. Two reads about 2 seconds apart reported 293.2 KB and then 508 KB for the same index, so it was actively growing at query time. Contrary to the framing of the question, no disk-space pressure is visible: the node reports 160.5 GB total on the /usr/share/elasticsearch/data overlay with 103.7 GB free (96.8 GB available), and all 21 app-187-* indices together account for well under 1 MB. The cluster is yellow with 20 unassigned shards, which matches one unassigned replica for each of the 20 yellow logs indices on a single-node cluster, not a capacity shortage; allocation explain was not run, so that attribution is an inference from shard counts and single-node topology. No historical disk-usage or index-growth data was available.

claims.text: app-187-metrics-analytics is the largest index matching app-187-*, at store.size 508kb (pri.store.size 508kb) with 5,000 documents and green health; it was the first row when sorting all matching indices by store size descending.

A second listing of pattern app-187-* sorted by store size descending again put app-187-metrics-analytics first at 293.2kb with 5,000 documents, and showed app-187-logs-01 through app-187-logs-20 each with 10 documents at 7.4-7.5kb and yellow health.

Index statistics for app-187-metrics-analytics show total store size_in_bytes 520263 for both primaries and total (519884 bytes of docs metadata, segments count 1), docs count 5000 with deleted 5000, and health green with 1 of 1 shards successful — the current footprint is approximately 508 KB.

The node serving these indices reports total 160,497,381,376 bytes (about 160.5 GB) on the / (overlay) mount backing /usr/share/elasticsearch/data, with 103,719,895,040 bytes free and 96,786,604,032 bytes available — roughly 65 percent free, far above the high-watermark free space of 16,049,738,137 bytes. No disk-exhaustion condition is visible at query time.

Cluster docker-cluster is yellow with 24 active primary shards, 24 active shards, 54.5 percent shards active, 20 unassigned shards, 0 unassigned primaries, 1 data node and 0 initializing or relocating shards — consistent with unassigned replicas on a single-node cluster rather than shards blocked for space (allocation explain was not run).

app-187-metrics-analytics appears to be under active write churn: its store size read 293.2 KB in one listing and 508 KB in another about two seconds later, and its stats show 5,000 live docs alongside 5,000 deleted docs in a single segment. This suggests continuous write-and-delete activity rather than historical accumulation, but a growth trend cannot be established from two nearby point-in-time reads.

The yellow cluster state and 20 unassigned shards are most likely the replicas of the 20 yellow app-187-logs-* indices unable to allocate on the single data node, i.e. a replica-count/topology configuration matter, not a symptom of running out of disk — this is inferred from shard counts and node count, not from allocation explain output.

If space must be reclaimed, focus on app-187-metrics-analytics (about 0.5 MB) only after confirming expectations, since the whole app-187-* set totals well under 1 MB against 103.7 GB free — the observed numbers do not support index size as the cause of disk pressure, so look outside Elasticsearch data (other mounts, volumes, container images, logs) if the host really is filling up.

Run allocation explain for the 20 unassigned shards and review the replica setting of the app-187-logs-* indices against the single-node topology, rather than treating the yellow status as a disk problem.

gaps: No historical disk-usage, index-growth or deletion history is available: the change_history integration is not connected, and every Elasticsearch tool here reports only state at the moment of the query, so when app-187-metrics-analytics grew and whether it will keep growing is unknown.
The two size readings for app-187-metrics-analytics (293.2kb then 508kb, roughly 2 seconds apart) are point-in-time values with no consistent baseline, so no growth rate is established.
elasticsearch_allocation_explain was not run, so the reason each of the 20 shards is unassigned is not directly observed; the replica-on-single-node explanation is an inference.
Whether the reported 'low disk space' applies to a different host, volume or cluster than the single node monitored here (bea971fdc0c6 / 172.17.0.2, docker-cluster) could not be determined.
No metric or log evidence was examined for services writing to these indices, so the producer of the write churn on app-187-metrics-analytics is unknown.
next_steps: Confirm which host/volume is actually reported low on disk; the Elasticsearch data mount here shows about 103.7 GB free of 160.5 GB.
If app-187-metrics-analytics growth matters, collect store.size over a window (for example via the cluster's own monitoring or scheduled _cat/indices snapshots) to establish a trend before acting.
Run allocation explain on the 20 unassigned shards and check index.number_of_replicas for app-187-logs-* before deciding whether to set replicas to 0 on the single-node cluster.
